newsitem.title: BRAZIL: EastTimor activist blasts "arms smuggler" Britain.
newsitem.headline: EastTimor activist blasts "arms smuggler" Britain.

text.p: East Timor activist Jose Ramos-Horta on Monday blasted Britain as the "greatest arms smuggler" to Indonesia, calling the sale of weapons to Indonesian occupiers of his homeland "immoral."

Ramos-Horta, joint winner of this year's Nobel Peace Prize, said during a visit to Brasilia that he had asked Brazil's President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to act as an envoy of East Timor in convincing countries like Britain to turn against Jakarta.
"Britain is the greatest arms smuggler to Indonesia," he charged, saying British weapons were being used to carry out "the crime of genocide" against the East Timorese.
He said East Timorese peace activists did not condemn economic engagement because economic growth was benefiting the middle classes, who were at "the forefront" of resistance.
"But we cannot condone arms sales to Indonesia or any other dictatorship. They are immoral," he said.
Ramos-Horta jointly won the Nobel Peace Prize last month with East Timor Roman Catholic Bishop Carlos Belo.
The former Portuguese colony has been torn by violence since Indonesia invaded the territory in 1975 and annexed it.

The United Nations still recognises Portugal as the administrative power and the U.N. General Assembly has in the past 21 years passed at least eight resolutions calling for Indonesian troops to withdraw.
The British media has repeatedly criticised London for allowing arms sales to Indonesia.

Last May, the annual general meeting of British Aerospace Plc dissolved into turmoil after protesters tried to throw eggs at the directors. The company denies its Hawk jets have been used against East Timorese demonstrators.

In Washington, 15 U.S. senators on Monday urged President Bill Clinton to raise the issue of in East Timor with Indonesian President Suharto when they meet next week at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Manila.

"We believe that the occasion of your meeting with President Suharto at the APEC summit offers an important opportunity to raise the issue of a United Nations-sponsored self-determination referendum for the people of East Timor," the senators wrote.
They also expressed concern about reports of substantial human rights violations by the Indonesian government in East Timor.
